practiceNotes: Use spaced retrieval for representations, assumptions, mechanisms and method selection. Separately assess complete proofs, executable programs, experiments and extended applications.
Require unfamiliar transfer tasks, delayed reassessment, reproducible artifacts, uncertainty budgets, negative results and explicit limitations.
Laboratory and field practice requires suitable facilities, supervision and local risk approval. Archived data can assess interpretation but cannot certify hands-on performance.
Human-participant, identifiable-data, vertebrate, ecological and genetic-manipulation projects require applicable consent, ethics review and authorization.
Use approved low-risk organisms and approved chemical procedures. Radiation, lasers, high voltage, pressure, cryogens and other hazardous apparatus require specialist supervision.
Security exercises require owned or explicitly authorized isolated systems; fault injection and robot testing must not endanger operational services or people.
Provided software is acceptable only where model specification, diagnostics and limitations are taught. Tool use does not substitute for separately promised implementation or proof.
This proposal does not confer clinical, industrial, engineering, environmental or laboratory operating authorization.

practice: Implement competing workload indexes and reconcile correctness proofs with measured costs.

outcomes.description: Prove recursive correctness and worst-case or amortized costs; generate adversarial structural tests and select workload-appropriate structures.
Implement lists, hashing, search trees, heaps and graph representations using explicit representation invariants.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Information Theory

includes: Entropy, source and channel coding, rate-distortion and finite-field codes

practice: Compress and transmit an unfamiliar finite-alphabet source and compare performance with theoretical bounds.

outcomes.description: Implement prefix compression and binary linear error-correcting codes; develop finite-field and syndrome operations locally and measure rate and decoding error.
Derive entropy, mutual information and elementary source, channel-capacity and rate-distortion bounds using typical sequences and explicit probability models.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Combinatorics
decks.description: Count structures and prove discrete results.

includes: Counting, finite graphs and extremal arguments

practice: Prove a graph bound and count the same unfamiliar family by two independent methods.

outcomes.description: Use bijections, inclusion-exclusion, recurrences and formal generating functions to count constrained objects.
Prove tree, connectivity, matching, coloring, planarity and elementary extremal or Ramsey results.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Linear Algebra

includes: Real and complex finite-dimensional linear algebra

practice: Recover a linear map from observations and compare exact, least-squares and truncated-SVD solutions.

outcomes.description: Calculate eigenstructure, Hermitian inner products, orthogonal projections, least squares, quadratic forms and singular-value decompositions.
Construct vector spaces, bases, linear maps and coordinate changes; prove dimension and map properties.
Solve matrix systems; calculate determinants, rank, null spaces and consistency conditions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Mathematical Logic

includes: First-order metatheory, computability and incompleteness

practice: Formalize an unfamiliar theory and present complete compactness and incompleteness arguments.

outcomes.description: Develop recursive functions, machine encodings, diagonalization and arithmetization locally; prove a precisely stated incompleteness theorem and distinguish semantic assumptions.
Develop formal proof systems; prove soundness, Henkin completeness and compactness and construct elementary models and expressibility counterexamples.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Number Theory

includes: Divisibility, congruences and integer equations
excludes: Advanced analytic and algebraic number theory

practice: Solve an unfamiliar integer equation and justify completeness or explicit limitations.

outcomes.description: Prove prime factorization and divisibility results; apply Euclidean algorithms, arithmetic functions, modular systems and quadratic reciprocity.
Solve bounded Diophantine problems using descent, congruences, continued fractions and rational approximation.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Real Analysis

includes: Real completeness, metric analysis and function convergence

practice: Prove and refute parameter-dependent convergence claims with complete estimates.

outcomes.description: Distinguish pointwise and uniform convergence; prove valid limit, derivative and integral interchanges and construct counterexamples.
Prove completeness, sequence convergence, compactness, continuity, differentiation and Riemann-integration results in real and metric settings.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Statistical Reasoning

includes: Study design, introductory inference and documented statistical software

practice: Analyze unfamiliar observational and randomized datasets with documented software and sensitivity checks.

outcomes.description: Design sampling and randomized comparisons; identify confounding, dependence, selection bias and misleading summaries.
Calculate intervals, tests and bootstrap estimates; fit simple regression and diagnose assumptions, residuals and causal limitations.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Electricity and Circuits
decks.description: Calculate and test elementary electrical systems.

includes: Point-charge electrostatics and low-voltage circuits

practice: Build a sensor-divider circuit and reconcile measured voltages with loading and uncertainty.

outcomes.description: Calculate point-charge forces, fields, potentials and capacitor energies using vector superposition.
Solve and build resistive networks using Kirchhoff laws; diagnose power limits, tolerances, meter loading and steady-state capacitance.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Mechanics

includes: Newtonian particles, rotation and gravitation

practice: Compare force-based and conservation-based predictions for an unfamiliar rolling or orbital problem.

outcomes.description: Calculate work, collisions, centers of mass, inertia, torque and rigid rotation with justified conservation assumptions.
Construct free-body diagrams and solve Cartesian and plane-polar motion; derive elementary central-force orbits using energy and angular momentum.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Optics Foundations

includes: Ray optics and algebraic wave-interference models

practice: Construct an image and interference experiment with independent dimensional and alignment checks.

outcomes.description: Use explicitly defined sinusoidal phase, polarization and path-difference models to calculate interference and single-slit diffraction scales.
Construct refraction and paraxial lens or mirror images; calculate magnification and identify geometric aberration limits.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Thermodynamics

includes: Macroscopic thermal laws and equilibrium criteria

practice: Evaluate an unfamiliar thermal cycle and identify irreversible losses through entropy accounting.

outcomes.description: Calculate equations of state, heat capacities, quasistatic work, entropy changes and engine or refrigerator efficiency bounds.
Use internal energy, enthalpy and free energies to predict equilibrium and simple phase transitions under explicit constraints.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Biochemistry

includes: Biomolecular structure, binding, catalysis and biochemical energetics

practice: Distinguish binding, catalytic and stability effects in an unfamiliar enzyme dataset.

outcomes.description: Calculate coupled biochemical free energies and redox driving forces with consistent standard states.
Derive the bounded steady-state Michaelis-Menten law algebraically and discriminate inhibition mechanisms with controlled enzyme assays.
Relate protein, nucleic-acid, carbohydrate and lipid structures to folding and recognition; calculate occupancy and cooperativity using explicit binding models.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Biostatistics

includes: Biological design and generalized or hierarchical models

practice: Preregister and analyze a blocked study with missingness and batch-adjustment sensitivity checks.

outcomes.description: Design factorial, blocked and repeated studies; evaluate power, confounding, pseudoreplication, multiplicity, missingness and batch effects.
Construct design matrices and likelihoods for linear, logistic, count and mixed models; fit, diagnose and reproduce analyses using documented software.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Ecology

includes: Populations, communities, ecosystems and field inference

practice: Conduct or reconstruct a field survey with detection-aware ecological comparisons.

outcomes.description: Design quadrat, transect and mark-recapture studies; estimate abundance and distinguish imperfect detection, sampling bias and ecological change.
Construct discrete growth and survival models; analyze competition, predation, mutualism, food webs, productivity and nutrient budgets.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Epidemiology

includes: Population-health study design and bounded transmission models

practice: Analyze an unfamiliar exposure study and intervention scenario without assuming a clinical qualification.

outcomes.description: Design cohort, case-control and randomized studies; calculate incidence, prevalence, risk and odds ratios and analyze confounding and selection.
Construct discrete susceptible-infected-recovered models and calculate reproduction thresholds; compare interventions with uncertainty and unequal population burdens.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Evolution

includes: Population change, phylogeny and macroevolution

practice: Compare population and phylogenetic explanations for an unfamiliar evolutionary pattern.

outcomes.description: Construct small parsimony trees and score explicit substitution-model likelihoods; evaluate homology, speciation, extinction and fossil or comparative evidence.
Calculate Hardy-Weinberg, selection and migration recurrences; distinguish drift and adaptation hypotheses.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Analytical Chemistry

includes: Coupled equilibria, quantitative analysis and validation

practice: Quantify an unknown mixture by independent methods and diagnose matrix effects.

outcomes.description: Formulate acid-base, precipitation, complexation and redox balances; solve bounded systems by approximation or taught bisection and check residuals.
Perform titrimetric, gravimetric and Beer-Lambert calibration analyses; quantify blanks, recovery, standard additions, detection limits, bias and uncertainty.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Kinetics

includes: Rate laws, mechanistic kinetics and temperature dependence

practice: Fit competing mechanisms and design a time or temperature experiment separating them.

outcomes.description: Derive pre-equilibrium and steady-state rate expressions; analyze Arrhenius behavior, catalysis, competing pathways and mechanistic nonuniqueness.
Derive integrated rate laws and fit time courses with documented nonlinear least squares, residual checks and parameter uncertainty.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Spectroscopy

includes: Small-molecule IR, mass and one-dimensional NMR inference

practice: Identify an unfamiliar molecule from incomplete spectra and propose a discriminating measurement.

outcomes.description: Assign formulas, functional groups, shifts, integrations and simple couplings; combine IR, mass and NMR evidence and identify unresolved alternatives.
Explain spectral axes, signal formation and resolution with explicit bounded vibration, ionization and nuclear-spin models.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Algorithms

includes: Design paradigms, graph algorithms and reductions

practice: Solve unfamiliar scheduling constraints with proofs, benchmarks and a reduction analysis.

outcomes.description: Design greedy, divide-and-conquer and dynamic-programming algorithms; prove correctness, solve recurrences and construct elementary hardness reductions.
Implement traversal, shortest paths, spanning trees and network flow; prove invariants and analyze time-space tradeoffs.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Databases

includes: Relational design, queries, transactions and alternative models

practice: Build a database, optimize its workload and reproduce then repair an isolation anomaly.

outcomes.description: Design schemas, constraints and normalized relations; write SQL and relational algebra and analyze indexes, joins and alternative document or graph models.
Analyze isolation, serializability, locking, logging and crash recovery using explicit transaction histories.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Graphics

includes: Geometry, rendering and image processing

practice: Build a renderer and verify it against constructed geometric and sampling reference scenes.

outcomes.description: Implement homogeneous transforms, camera projection, ray intersections, triangle rasterization and depth testing in three-dimensional scenes.
Implement local-illumination ray tracing, convolution, resampling and curve interpolation; diagnose aliasing, color-space and visibility artifacts.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Human-Computer Interaction

includes: User research, accessibility, prototypes and evaluation

practice: Redesign an accessible interface using an approved or simulated usability study.

outcomes.description: Translate user observations into task models, interaction prototypes and accessibility requirements.
Conduct usability and controlled comparisons; integrate qualitative and quantitative evidence and justify consent, manipulation and exclusion tradeoffs.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Operating Systems

includes: Processes, synchronization, memory, storage and system interfaces

practice: Extend an instructional kernel and test adversarial schedules, page faults and crashes.

outcomes.description: Implement scheduling and synchronization; reason about atomicity, races, deadlock and concurrent invariants.
Implement bounded allocation, virtual-memory and filesystem mechanisms; analyze protection, system calls, I/O and crash consistency.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Programming Languages

includes: Semantics, interpreters, types and abstraction

practice: Implement a typed language with two evaluation strategies and validate semantic differences.

outcomes.description: Define operational semantics and interpreters with environments, closures and mutation; compare functional, object-oriented and declarative abstraction.
Implement static typing and prove bounded progress and preservation by structural induction; compare evaluation strategies.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Software Engineering

includes: Requirements, modularity, testing and delivery

practice: Deliver a reviewed team change from negotiated requirements through release and retrospective.

outcomes.description: Use version control, review, refactoring, integration tests, automated builds and release procedures; diagnose regressions and operational risks.
Elicit requirements, define acceptance tests and modular interfaces, and justify privacy, accessibility and stakeholder tradeoffs.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Abstract Algebra

includes: Groups, rings, ideals and field extensions

practice: Classify an unfamiliar finite structure and prove its quotient and extension properties.

outcomes.description: Prove group, action and homomorphism results; calculate quotients and finite-group structure using Sylow theorems.
Construct rings, ideals, quotient fields and finite extensions; prove factorization properties and determine minimal polynomials and degrees.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Differential Equations

includes: ODE solutions, systems and qualitative dynamics

practice: Derive a coupled flow model and verify solutions, phase portraits and step-size behavior.

outcomes.description: Construct phase portraits, linearize equilibria and classify stability and elementary bifurcations; compare analytic solutions with Euler steps.
Solve separable, linear first-order and forced constant-coefficient equations; solve coupled systems with eigenvectors and matrix exponentials.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Markov Processes

includes: Finite Markov chains, Poisson processes and elementary queues

practice: Analyze an unfamiliar reliability or queue model and check normalization and balance.

outcomes.description: Calculate finite-chain transitions, stationary distributions, absorption probabilities and hitting times by conditioning and linear systems.
Derive exponential waiting and Poisson-count models; formulate finite continuous-time generators and bounded queue balance equations.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Measure Theory

includes: Measure construction and Lebesgue integration

practice: Construct convergence counterexamples and prove a new parameter-dependent integral result.

outcomes.description: Construct sigma-algebras, outer measures, measures and measurable functions; distinguish null-set and measurability issues.
Develop Lebesgue and product integration; prove convergence theorems and apply Fubini, Tonelli and Radon-Nikodym with verified hypotheses.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Multivariable Calculus
decks.description: Calculate functions and fields in space.

includes: Multivariable derivatives, coordinates and vector integration

practice: Calculate a three-dimensional flux and extremum using independent coordinate and theorem checks.

outcomes.description: Compute gradients, Jacobians and Hessians; apply chain rules, Taylor approximations and constrained extrema.
Evaluate multiple, line and surface integrals in Cartesian, cylindrical and spherical coordinates; apply Green, Stokes and divergence theorems.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Numerical Methods

includes: Numerical error, algebraic algorithms, quadrature and ODE integration

practice: Build a tested solver collection including ill-conditioned and unstable counterexamples.

outcomes.description: Implement root finding, pivoted solves, least squares, interpolation and quadrature; distinguish conditioning, stability, roundoff and truncation.
Formulate initial-value state models; implement Euler and Runge-Kutta methods and evaluate residuals, convergence and stability regions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Topology

includes: Point-set topology and space constructions

practice: Classify unfamiliar quotient spaces with proofs and counterexamples.

outcomes.description: Analyze products, quotients and homeomorphisms; construct counterexamples and topological obstructions.
Construct topologies and continuous maps; prove compactness, connectedness, separation and countability properties and distinguish metric special cases.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Observational Astronomy
decks.description: Infer celestial properties from remote evidence.

includes: Astronomical coordinates, photometry and spectral inference

practice: Estimate unfamiliar stellar properties from calibrated images and spectra with selection-aware uncertainty.

outcomes.description: Transform celestial coordinates and calculate angular scales, parallax, flux, luminosity, magnitudes and Doppler velocities.
Calibrate images and spectra using documented tools; fit bounded blackbody and line models and assess extinction, backgrounds and selection bias.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Behavioral Ecology

includes: Ethology, behavior measurement and evolutionary decision models

practice: Analyze an unfamiliar social or foraging behavior using distinct proximate and evolutionary tests.

outcomes.description: Calculate bounded foraging, game and inclusive-fitness predictions; compare mating, cooperation and life-history explanations using comparative evidence.
Construct ethograms and sampling protocols; test learning, communication and behavioral-development hypotheses while controlling observer and motivational bias.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Conservation Biology

includes: Biodiversity risk, connectivity and conservation decisions

practice: Prepare a conservation dossier with population projections, monitoring triggers and stakeholder tradeoffs.

outcomes.description: Estimate biodiversity and extinction risk using detection-aware surveys and locally derived stage-structured population matrices.
Compare reserves, connectivity, harvest, restoration and invasive-species control; justify adaptive management considering uncertainty, local knowledge and distributional impacts.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Metabolism
decks.description: Account for biological matter and energy.

includes: Central pathways, bioenergetics and metabolic integration

practice: Reconcile metabolite and isotope data and predict an unfamiliar enzyme or nutrient perturbation.

outcomes.description: Calculate respiration and photosynthesis ATP balances; explain chemiosmosis, pathway regulation and nutrient or tissue-level adaptation.
Trace carbon, nitrogen and reducing equivalents through carbohydrate, lipid, amino-acid and nucleotide metabolism; interpret simple isotope-label patterns.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Molecular Biology

includes: Information flow, regulation and molecular manipulation

practice: Design a reporter experiment distinguishing expression, processing and protein-function defects.

outcomes.description: Design PCR, gels, cloning, sequencing, reporters and bounded genome-editing experiments with specificity, controls, rescue and interpretation criteria.
Explain replication, repair, recombination, transcription, RNA processing, translation and gene regulation using sequence and molecular representations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Thermodynamics

includes: Chemical potential, nonideality and phase equilibria

practice: Construct a nonideal binary phase diagram and test model and standard-state sensitivity.

outcomes.description: Calculate activities, fugacities, reaction equilibria and binary phase diagrams; assess stability, standard states and temperature dependence.
Derive chemical potentials, partial molar properties, Maxwell relations and Gibbs-Duhem constraints from thermodynamic differentials.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Electrochemistry

includes: Accessible electrode energetics, kinetics, transport and measurements

practice: Separate kinetic, resistive and transport losses in unfamiliar polarization and impedance data.

outcomes.description: Develop Gibbs-energy and Nernst electrode models with standard states; calculate cell voltages, concentration effects and reference conversions.
Apply explicitly taught Butler-Volmer, Tafel, diffusion-layer and complex-impedance circuit models; interpret voltammetry, corrosion, batteries and sensor limitations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Environmental Chemistry

includes: Air, water and soil chemistry and environmental decisions

practice: Construct a contaminant budget and defend a monitoring and remediation plan.

outcomes.description: Design preservation, sampling and analytical controls; compare remediation using exposure, uncertainty, lifecycle boundaries and unequal environmental burdens.
Calculate speciation, partitioning, residence times and first-order compartment budgets; explain atmospheric photochemistry and environmental redox transformations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Instrumental Methods

includes: Chromatographic, electrophoretic, optical and mass-instrument working methods

practice: Develop and validate a separation-detection assay for an unfamiliar mixture.

outcomes.description: Explain sources, analyzers and detectors; select sampling, calibration and orthogonal identification procedures for optical and mass instruments.
Design separations using partition, retention, plate-height, selectivity and resolution models; interpret chromatograms and electropherograms.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Synthesis

includes: Selective transformations, retrosynthesis and verification

practice: Compare routes to an unfamiliar target and execute an approved step with complete characterization.

outcomes.description: Predict carbonyl, aromatic, organometallic and redox selectivity; construct retrosyntheses using carbon-carbon disconnections, protecting groups and functional interconversions.
Design reaction setup, workup and purification; verify identity, stereochemistry, purity, yield and competing-pathway evidence.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organometallic Reactivity

includes: Coordination reactions and organometallic catalytic inference

practice: Infer a catalytic cycle from unfamiliar spectra and rate data and propose a discriminating intervention.

outcomes.description: Construct catalytic cycles and derive competing rate laws; combine speciation, stereochemical and kinetic controls to identify turnover limitations.
Use electron counting and elementary orbital pictures to predict substitution, oxidative addition, reductive elimination, insertion and electron-transfer reactions.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Polymer Chemistry

includes: Polymer synthesis, distributions and bounded property models

practice: Choose a polymer route and reconcile molecular-weight, thermal and mechanical measurements.

outcomes.description: Use locally developed chain-statistics, mixing and spring-dashpot models to interpret solution behavior, glass transition, crystallinity and viscoelastic data.
Design step-growth, chain-growth and copolymerization routes; calculate conversion, architecture, molecular-mass averages and dispersity.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Artificial Intelligence

includes: Search, knowledge, probabilistic inference and finite decisions

practice: Compare search and uncertain planning agents on an unfamiliar finite task.

outcomes.description: Formulate finite Markov decision processes; implement value iteration and tabular reinforcement learning and assess reward and risk choices.
Implement heuristic and adversarial search, constraint propagation, rule inference and finite Bayesian-network inference; explain pruning and admissibility.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Theory of Computation

includes: Automata, grammars, computability and complexity

practice: Classify unfamiliar languages and decision problems with constructions and reductions.

outcomes.description: Construct and transform automata, regular expressions, grammars and pushdown machines; prove expressiveness limits.
Construct Turing computations; prove undecidability by diagonalization and reductions and NP-completeness through polynomial reductions and certificates.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Vision

includes: Image formation, features, motion and geometric reconstruction

practice: Recover geometry and motion from unfamiliar calibrated images with outlier and degeneracy tests.

outcomes.description: Calibrate cameras; estimate homographies, epipolar geometry and stereo depth using least squares and taught RANSAC; diagnose ambiguity and reprojection error.
Implement filtering, gradients, feature matching, segmentation and optical flow from explicit image-formation and brightness assumptions.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Distributed Systems
decks.description: Build coherent services under partial failure.

includes: Distributed models, consensus, replication and operation

practice: Validate a replicated service's histories during partitions, crashes and delayed messages.

outcomes.description: Implement replicated logs and distributed transactions; fault-test recovery, quorums, retries, idempotence, backpressure and observability.
Model clocks, asynchronous executions, failures and consistency; prove bounded safety and liveness and explain consensus impossibility assumptions.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Machine Learning

includes: Predictive learning, representations and responsible evaluation

practice: Implement competing learners on unfamiliar data with reproducible validation and error audits.

outcomes.description: Design leakage-free validation, calibration and subgroup error analysis; evaluate imbalance, privacy, harms and distribution shift.
Derive and implement regression, regularization, trees, clustering, PCA and small neural networks with gradient descent and backpropagation.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Parallel Computing

includes: Shared-memory, message-passing and data-parallel computation

practice: Parallelize a sparse or stencil workload and test correctness and scaling across configurations.

outcomes.description: Implement task, data and message-passing parallelism using synchronization, reductions, partitioning and explicit communication protocols.
Analyze work-span, locality, load balance and communication costs; diagnose races and reconcile scaling measurements with models.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Robotics and Control

includes: Robot kinematics, state estimation, feedback and planning

practice: Simulate an unfamiliar robot with noisy sensing, obstacle planning and feedback tracking.

outcomes.description: Develop state-space, PID and pole-placement models; derive Gaussian conditioning and Kalman filtering and test controllability, observability and stability.
Construct rigid transforms and planar or spatial manipulator kinematics; solve bounded inverse kinematics using Jacobians and least squares.
Implement collision checks and configuration-space search or sampling; validate tracking, localization uncertainty and safe-stop decisions.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Security and Privacy

includes: Threats, defenses, privacy and cryptographic use

practice: Audit an isolated application and verify mitigations with abuse-case regression tests.

outcomes.description: Develop needed modular arithmetic; explain encryption, authentication, signatures and key exchange and diagnose standard-primitive protocol misuse.
Threat-model systems; reproduce authorized memory, injection and authentication attacks; implement defenses and justify privacy, disclosure and response decisions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Algebraic Geometry
decks.description: Connect polynomial equations and geometric structure.

includes: Commutative algebra and affine/projective geometry foundations

practice: Analyze an unfamiliar polynomial variety through ideals, elimination, local coordinates and singularity calculations.

outcomes.description: Develop Noetherian rings, localization, prime ideals, integral extensions and Gröbner reduction; prove bounded Nullstellensatz and elimination results.
Construct affine and projective varieties, morphisms, local rings and elementary affine schemes; compute dimension, tangent spaces and singularities.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Algebraic Topology

includes: Fundamental groups, coverings and homology

practice: Calculate invariants of unfamiliar glued spaces and prove an obstruction.

outcomes.description: Develop chain complexes and exact sequences locally; compute simplicial and singular homology and prove bounded invariance and fixed-point results.
Calculate fundamental groups and covering relationships using homotopy and van Kampen; prove nonretraction consequences.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Complex Analysis

includes: Holomorphic functions, residues and conformal methods

practice: Evaluate a parameterized real integral and solve a transformed planar boundary problem.

outcomes.description: Prove holomorphic-function and Cauchy integral results; analyze power and Laurent series, singularities and analytic continuation.
Evaluate contour and real integrals with residue estimates; solve bounded harmonic problems using conformal maps.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Curves and Surfaces

includes: Curves, surfaces and intrinsic geometry

practice: Compare intrinsic and extrinsic geometry and calculate geodesics on unfamiliar surfaces.

outcomes.description: Calculate curve frames, curvature and torsion and surface tangent planes, fundamental forms, Gaussian and mean curvature.
Derive parametrized-surface geodesic equations by local energy variation; calculate intrinsic distances and parallel transport.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Functional Analysis

includes: Banach and Hilbert analysis and variational foundations

practice: Prove an unfamiliar operator result and construct a spectral or variational approximation.

outcomes.description: Prove bounded forms of Hahn-Banach, uniform boundedness, open mapping and compact self-adjoint spectral results; establish coercive variational existence.
Construct Banach, Hilbert and Lp spaces; prove completeness, projection and duality results.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Graduate Algebra

includes: Modules, Galois theory and finite-group representations

practice: Determine a polynomial's Galois structure and decompose an unfamiliar group representation.

outcomes.description: Prove Galois correspondence; calculate splitting fields, solvability and constructibility.
Construct modules, tensor products and exact sequences; prove and apply structure theorems over principal ideal domains.
Construct finite-group representations and character tables; prove orthogonality and decomposition results.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Graduate Probability

includes: Measure probability, conditioning, martingales and random processes

practice: Construct an unfamiliar process and prove a stopped-expectation or convergence claim.

outcomes.description: Construct probability spaces and conditional expectations; prove bounded laws of large numbers, central limits and convergence results.
Develop filtrations, stopping times, Markov kernels and martingales; prove optional-stopping and convergence results and construct Brownian motion.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Mathematical Statistics

includes: Continuous probability and parametric inference

practice: Compare exact, asymptotic and Bayesian uncertainty for an unfamiliar sampling model.

outcomes.description: Derive likelihood, moment and conjugate Bayesian estimators, information bounds, likelihood-ratio tests and linear-model inference; state asymptotic assumptions.
Calculate joint, marginal and transformed densities, moments and sampling distributions using multiple integration and Jacobians.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Optimization

includes: Linear, smooth and convex optimization

practice: Solve allocation and fitting problems with certificates and sensitivity analyses.

outcomes.description: Implement gradient, Newton, projected and line-search methods; use documented LP solvers and diagnose infeasibility, scaling and convergence.
Formulate linear and convex programs; derive optimality conditions, KKT systems and dual certificates under explicit regularity assumptions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Partial Differential Equations
decks.description: Solve field evolution and boundary problems.

includes: Classical linear PDE and Fourier methods

practice: Solve a forced heat problem by expansion and convolution and verify all data.

outcomes.description: Classify transport, heat, wave and elliptic models; solve characteristics and separated rectangular or radial boundary problems.
Develop Fourier series, transforms, convolution and Green functions; solve source problems and establish bounded uniqueness and conservation checks.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Analytical Mechanics

includes: Variational, Hamiltonian and nonlinear mechanics

practice: Analyze a constrained coupled system in Lagrangian and Hamiltonian representations.

outcomes.description: Derive Euler-Lagrange equations, constrained generalized coordinates and Noether conservation laws through explicit action variations.
Construct Hamiltonians, Poisson brackets and canonical transformations; analyze normal modes, separatrices, resonance and bounded chaotic dynamics.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Astrophysics

includes: Stellar structure, galactic dynamics and bounded cosmology

practice: Compare stellar or galactic models with an unfamiliar observational dataset.

outcomes.description: Infer galactic mass profiles; apply explicitly developed Friedmann-model relations to expansion, dark-matter and cosmic-background evidence.
Construct hydrostatic, energy-generation and radiative-transport stellar equations; analyze bounded stellar models, evolution and compact-object evidence.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Elastic Continua

includes: Linear elastic stress, strain, energy and waves

practice: Calculate deformation and vibration of an unfamiliar elastic component and check energy and boundaries.

outcomes.description: Derive strain, stress, Hooke tensors and equilibrium equations; solve bounded extension, torsion and beam-bending problems with compatibility checks.
Derive elastic energy and longitudinal or transverse wave equations; analyze boundary modes and stability under stated small-strain assumptions.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Electromagnetism

includes: Static fields, Maxwell equations and radiation

practice: Solve unfamiliar dielectric and radiating-source problems with boundary and energy checks.

outcomes.description: Apply Maxwell equations to induction, AC networks, plane-wave interfaces and retarded dipole radiation; calculate energy and momentum flow.
Solve electrostatic and magnetostatic problems using potentials, symmetry, images, multipoles and material boundary conditions.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Fluid Mechanics

includes: Fluid balances, viscous flow, waves and compressibility

practice: Predict unfamiliar pressure-driven flow and compare exact profiles, scaling and observations.

outcomes.description: Derive control-volume and local mass, momentum and energy balances using stress tensors and constitutive assumptions.
Solve hydrostatic, potential, channel and creeping flows; apply boundary-layer scaling, dimensionless regimes, surface-wave and shock-jump models.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Mechanics

includes: Quantum postulates, wave equations, spin and central potentials

practice: Solve an unfamiliar piecewise potential and spin experiment using analytic state and spectral calculations.

outcomes.description: Derive angular-momentum algebra, spin measurements and spherical separation of central potentials, including hydrogenic spectra.
Solve one-dimensional wells, barriers and oscillators with matching and probability-current checks.
Represent complex states and observables; calculate normalization, uncertainty, probabilities and unitary evolution in finite and wavefunction representations.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Statistical Mechanics

includes: Ensembles, fluctuations and ideal quantum statistics

practice: Calculate unfamiliar microscopic-model observables and compare thermodynamic limits.

outcomes.description: Derive microcanonical, canonical and grand-canonical distributions; calculate partition functions, thermodynamic observables and fluctuations.
Develop occupation-state counting and derive classical, Bose and Fermi laws; calculate ideal gases, phonons and elementary phase-transition models.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Oscillations and Waves

includes: Oscillators, normal modes and classical wave equations

practice: Predict resonances and wave patterns for a new bounded medium and verify its boundary conditions.

outcomes.description: Solve damped, forced and coupled oscillators; calculate resonance, normal modes and energy transfer.
Derive one-dimensional string and acoustic wave models; solve traveling and standing waves and explain dispersion and boundary matching.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Animal Physiology

includes: Comparative animal transport, regulation and integration

practice: Discriminate physiological mechanisms in a comparative stress-response dataset.

outcomes.description: Explain endocrine, renal, thermal, muscular and reproductive regulation; predict integrated exercise, fasting and environmental-stress responses.
Apply taught pressure-flow, diffusion, clearance and mass-balance models to circulation, respiration, digestion and excretion.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Bioinformatics

includes: Sequence algorithms and reproducible genomic inference

practice: Implement an alignment kernel and analyze unfamiliar reads with uncertainty and provenance reporting.

outcomes.description: Implement pairwise alignment by dynamic programming; explain scoring, indexing and heuristic-search tradeoffs.
Run documented quality, mapping, assembly, variant and expression workflows; evaluate annotation, enrichment, multiplicity, coverage, batch effects and provenance.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Developmental Biology

includes: Patterning, lineage and morphogenesis

practice: Infer a developmental mechanism from lineage data and design a decisive rescue.

outcomes.description: Design lineage-tracing, transplantation, perturbation and rescue experiments distinguishing specification, determination and environmental effects.
Explain induction, positional information, fate stabilization, cell mechanics, migration and regeneration in animal and plant development.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Immunology

includes: Innate and adaptive immunity and immune assays

practice: Separate recognition and effector failures in an unfamiliar immune-response dataset.

outcomes.description: Design and interpret ELISA, flow-cytometry and functional assays with gating, specificity, compensation and control strategies.
Explain innate sensing, antigen presentation, receptor diversification, selection, tolerance, effector function and memory; distinguish autoimmunity, allergy and evasion.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Microbiology and Virology

includes: Microbial physiology, identification, resistance and viruses

practice: Characterize an approved isolate and interpret an archived viral assay with explicit controls.

outcomes.description: Compare bacterial, archaeal and microbial-eukaryotic physiology, ecological roles, gene transfer and antimicrobial resistance.
Perform approved aseptic culture, staining, viable counts and biochemical identification; interpret growth curves and contamination controls.
Trace viral entry, genome expression, replication, assembly and transmission using locally developed genome-class models; interpret plaque and host-range evidence.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Plant Biology

includes: Plant anatomy, transport, photosynthesis and responses

practice: Separate anatomical, stomatal and biochemical explanations of plant treatment responses.

outcomes.description: Identify tissues, meristems and reproductive structures; calculate water potential and gas exchange and explain mineral, phloem and photosynthetic processes.
Predict hormonal, photoperiodic, developmental and stress responses; design controlled growth and transport experiments.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Systems Biology

includes: Cellular networks, metabolic constraints and dynamical inference

practice: Fit a cellular network and predict a held-out perturbation that tests identifiability.

outcomes.description: Fit dynamical parameters; calculate sensitivities, structural nonidentifiability and bootstrap uncertainty and design resolving perturbations.
Build stoichiometric and regulatory networks; derive mass-action ODEs and solve flux-balance, feedback and stability problems.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Theoretical Ecology

includes: Ecological dynamics, spatial stochasticity and hidden-state inference

practice: Fit an interacting-population model and test perturbation predictions under imperfect detection.

outcomes.description: Derive consumer-resource, competition and stage models; analyze stability and bifurcation and implement finite-patch stochastic dispersal models.
Specify ecological state and observation models; fit documented likelihoods and test persistence, identifiability and held-out predictions.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Advanced Analytical Chemistry

includes: Multidimensional structural evidence and chemometrics

practice: Validate a complex-mixture assay with independent samples and complementary structural measurements.

outcomes.description: Construct multivariate calibration and spectral decomposition using documented algorithms; validate identification, detection, matrix effects and calibration transfer.
Develop pulse-correlation and fragmentation models for two-dimensional NMR and tandem MS; resolve bounded complex-mixture assignments.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Industrial Chemistry

includes: Reactors, separations, flowsheets and process judgment

practice: Compare reactor-separation flowsheets including heat-removal and upset-condition tradeoffs.

outcomes.description: Derive batch, stirred-tank and plug-flow material and energy balances; calculate conversion, residence time and thermal stability.
Calculate staged distillation, extraction and recycle; compare flowsheets through yield, energy, waste, lifecycle assumptions and process-hazard scenarios.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Materials Chemistry

includes: Crystallography, defects, synthesis and characterization

practice: Plan an approved synthesis and infer phase composition from complementary characterization.

outcomes.description: Plan ceramic, solution and film synthesis using phase stability, nucleation and diffusion-length models; combine thermal, microscopic and compositional validation.
Construct reciprocal lattices and Miller indices; derive Bragg and structure-factor relations and index bounded powder patterns and defect equilibria.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Quantum Chemistry

includes: Molecular electronic approximations and spectra

practice: Iterate a supplied-integral molecular model and compare calculated energies and spectra.

outcomes.description: Construct Born-Oppenheimer Hamiltonians and antisymmetric orbital states; derive variational and Hartree-Fock matrix procedures and compare correlation and density-functional approximations.
Calculate rotational, vibrational and electronic transitions and selection rules for bounded molecular models; diagnose basis and approximation errors.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Soft Matter and Interfaces

includes: Statistical polymers, colloids, interfaces and relaxation

practice: Explain an unfamiliar soft-material phase diagram and relaxation spectrum with competing models.

outcomes.description: Derive bounded Rouse, viscoelastic and colloidal relaxation models; infer timescales from rheology and dynamic-scattering data.
Derive chain entropy, mixing free energies, interfacial tension, adsorption and colloidal interaction models; predict phase and scattering behavior.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Advanced Algorithms

includes: Randomized, approximation, streaming and online algorithms

practice: Prove and benchmark an unfamiliar approximation or streaming algorithm on adversarial inputs.

outcomes.description: Design approximation and online algorithms using relaxations, primal-dual and charging arguments; prove parameterized, time-space and approximation reductions.
Derive concentration bounds and analyze randomized hashing, sampling and streaming with explicit failure probabilities.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Advanced Learning Methods

includes: Advanced neural, latent-variable and sequential learning methods

practice: Implement and validate a latent or sequential learner with gradient checks and held-out perturbations.

outcomes.description: Implement automatic-differentiation graphs and convolutional, attention and sequence models; diagnose gradient, optimization and calibration failures.
Derive and implement EM, variational latent models and policy-gradient learning; evaluate uncertainty, representation and distribution-shift limitations.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Advanced Robotics

includes: Visual state estimation, SLAM and constrained optimal control

practice: Build a visual navigation simulation and audit estimation consistency and constrained-control failures.

outcomes.description: Derive dynamic-programming, LQR and model-predictive control objectives; implement constrained trajectory optimization and evaluate robustness and failure recovery.
Derive nonlinear filtering, factor-graph smoothing and bundle adjustment; implement bounded visual SLAM and test gauge freedom, observability and consistency.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Compilers

includes: Compiler frontends, dataflow and code generation

practice: Build an end-to-end compiler with differential and generated tests.

outcomes.description: Implement fixed-point dataflow optimization, instruction selection, calling conventions and register allocation; validate semantic preservation against an interpreter.
Implement lexing, parsing, resolution and type checking; construct control-flow and intermediate representations.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Cryptographic Theory

includes: Security games, reductions and foundational constructions

practice: Prove or break a proposed construction using explicit games and executable small-instance checks.

outcomes.description: Construct and analyze encryption, authentication, signatures and key exchange from stated computational assumptions; demonstrate failures when assumptions change.
Define negligible advantage, indistinguishability, pseudorandomness and adversarial games; construct hybrid and reduction proofs.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Formal Methods

includes: Program logic, model checking and proof tools

practice: Verify a stateful program with manual arguments, executable checks and counterexample analysis.

outcomes.description: Define transition and temporal models; implement bounded checking and use documented solvers or proof assistants while auditing abstractions and trust.
Specify preconditions, postconditions, invariants and termination measures; prove correctness using Hoare-style rules.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Learning Theory

includes: Statistical learning guarantees and impossibility

practice: Prove a guarantee for an unfamiliar model family and construct an assumption-breaking counterexample.

outcomes.description: Prove concentration, symmetrization and finite-class or capacity-based generalization bounds with explicit measurability and sampling assumptions.
Derive bounded minimax lower bounds and stability results; distinguish approximation, estimation, optimization and distribution-shift errors.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Algebraic Number Theory

includes: Number fields, algebraic integers, ideals and arithmetic invariants

practice: Determine prime splitting and ideal-class behavior in an unfamiliar quadratic or small-degree field.

outcomes.description: Develop Dedekind ideal factorization, ramification, units and class groups; calculate prime splitting and prove bounded class-number results.
Compute algebraic integers, integral bases, traces, norms and discriminants; derive embeddings and bounded lattice estimates.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Analytic Number Theory

includes: Arithmetic sums, Dirichlet series and prime-distribution foundations

practice: Estimate an unfamiliar arithmetic sum by elementary and complex-analytic methods and compare errors.

outcomes.description: Develop zeta and Dirichlet L-series, Euler products and character orthogonality; apply continuation, contour methods and Tauberian arguments in bounded prime-distribution results.
Derive partial summation, convolution and elementary sieve estimates; bound unfamiliar arithmetic sums with explicit error terms.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Graduate Analysis and PDE

includes: Distributions, Sobolev spaces and weak PDE approximation

practice: Prove weak well-posedness and validate a finite-element refinement study.

outcomes.description: Derive and implement Galerkin and elementary finite-element methods; prove bounded error estimates and verify mesh convergence.
Construct distributions, weak derivatives, Sobolev spaces and traces; prove bounded elliptic and evolutionary existence using coercivity, compactness and energy estimates.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Manifolds

includes: Smooth manifolds, forms, metrics and curvature

practice: Compute invariant integrals and curvature independently in overlapping charts.

outcomes.description: Calculate metrics, connections, geodesics and curvature tensors and prove coordinate invariance of geometric conclusions.
Construct atlases, tangent and cotangent bundles, vector fields and tensors; calculate forms, pullbacks and exterior derivatives and prove bounded Stokes results.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Graduate Statistical Inference

includes: Asymptotic, decision-theoretic and nonparametric inference

practice: Prove and empirically interrogate an unfamiliar estimator's risk and coverage.

outcomes.description: Prove estimator consistency, asymptotic normality and delta-method results; develop bounded posterior-consistency arguments.
Compare admissible, minimax and Bayesian risk; derive kernel, resampling and regularized nonparametric procedures with bias-variance and coverage analysis.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Stochastic Calculus

includes: Ito integration, stochastic differential equations and simulation

practice: Solve and simulate an unfamiliar diffusion with convergence and hitting-time checks.

outcomes.description: Construct L2 Ito integrals, prove the isometry and Ito formula, and solve bounded stochastic differential equations with stated existence assumptions.
Implement Euler-Maruyama and compare strong and weak errors, stopping behavior and analytic moment predictions.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Advanced Quantum Mechanics
decks.description: Analyze quantum systems beyond exact solutions.

includes: Approximation, scattering and composite quantum systems

practice: Compare approximation methods for unfamiliar scattering and reduced-state dynamics.

outcomes.description: Derive stationary and time-dependent perturbation, variational and semiclassical approximations and transition rates.
Construct identical-particle and tensor-product states, reduced density matrices and bounded master equations; calculate entanglement and decoherence.
Calculate three-dimensional partial-wave and Born scattering using Green functions; verify cross sections and unitarity.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Advanced Statistical Physics

includes: Sampling, criticality, kinetic relaxation and response

practice: Simulate a phase transition and relaxation process and distinguish physical from sampling timescales.

outcomes.description: Derive Landau and elementary renormalization scaling, kinetic and Langevin relaxation, and fluctuation-response relations for bounded models.
Implement Metropolis sampling and master-equation dynamics; prove detailed balance and diagnose equilibration, autocorrelation and finite-size errors.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Computational Physics

includes: Forward particle and finite-difference field simulation

practice: Validate a new particle and field model against exact solutions and conservation tests.

outcomes.description: Implement heat, wave and Poisson finite-difference solvers; derive bounded stability conditions and verify grid convergence and boundary consistency.
Implement particle and oscillator models with conservation-aware integration and compare trajectory, phase and energy errors.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Condensed Matter

includes: Lattices, bands, transport and ordered phases

practice: Reconcile diffraction, heat-capacity and transport data for an unfamiliar solid.

outcomes.description: Derive Bloch and tight-binding bands; calculate carrier statistics, semiconductor junctions and bounded transport coefficients.
Analyze magnetic, superconducting and structural order using symmetry, order parameters and explicit phenomenological free energies.
Construct reciprocal lattices and calculate diffraction, lattice vibrations and phonon thermodynamics.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Experimental Physics

includes: Instrumentation, signal analysis and physical inference

practice: Build a resonance or optical acquisition chain with calibrated spectral and model-comparison evidence.

outcomes.description: Use lock-in detection and weighted physical-model fits; design uncertainty budgets and controls separating systematic error from model failure.
Build calibrated sensor, op-amp and filter chains; implement discrete Fourier analysis and diagnose sampling, aliasing, grounding and noise.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Nuclear and Particle Physics

includes: Nuclei, particles, reactions and detector evidence

practice: Identify an unfamiliar decay or collision process from archived calibrated detector data.

outcomes.description: Reconstruct invariant masses and thresholds; explain radiation-matter interactions and correct detector spectra for efficiency, background and counting uncertainty.
Calculate binding, shell structure, tunneling decay, reaction energetics and cross sections; classify particle interactions and conservation or selection rules.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Optical Physics

includes: Fourier optics, lasers, coherence and detection

practice: Design an unfamiliar optical sensor and verify propagation, threshold and noise budgets.

outcomes.description: Develop transition and laser rate equations; calculate thresholds, bounded nonlinear mixing, coherence, resolution and photodetection noise.
Derive paraxial propagation, Gaussian beams, resonator stability and imaging transfer functions using Fourier optics.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Plasma Foundations

includes: Plasma particles, screening, fluid waves and MHD

practice: Compare particle and fluid predictions for an unfamiliar plasma regime.

outcomes.description: Derive two-fluid and MHD models; solve bounded plasma-wave dispersion, equilibrium and ideal-instability problems.
Calculate gyromotion, drifts and adiabatic invariants; derive Debye screening and identify magnetization and collective scales.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Advanced Cell Biology

includes: Advanced regulation, single-cell evidence and causal perturbation

practice: Develop a single-cell perturbation study that distinguishes correlated states from regulatory causes.

outcomes.description: Analyze chromatin, RNA regulation, proteostasis and organelle dynamics using competing mechanisms and temporal perturbation or rescue evidence.
Design and analyze single-cell expression, accessibility and imaging studies; distinguish batch, dropout, lineage, state and fate effects.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Disease and Biotechnology

includes: Disease mechanisms and biotechnology translation

practice: Prepare an unfamiliar intervention dossier integrating mechanism, population evidence and benefit-risk judgments.

outcomes.description: Explain infectious, genetic, metabolic and neoplastic disease mechanisms; assess model-organism, organoid and population evidence.
Design bounded diagnostic, therapeutic or engineered-biological workflows; justify efficacy, safety, consent, access, dual-use and experimental translation decisions.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Neuroscience

includes: Neural excitability, circuits, plasticity and behavioral experiments

practice: Analyze neural and behavioral responses and propose interventions separating competing coding hypotheses.

outcomes.description: Trace sensory, motor and autonomic circuits; evaluate coding, plasticity and learning using electrophysiological and behavioral controls.
Develop Nernst and equivalent-circuit membrane models; calculate resting and synaptic potentials and explain action-potential generation.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Population Genetics

includes: Finite-population, genealogy and genomic inference methods

practice: Test a selection claim against alternative demographic explanations in unfamiliar genomic data.

outcomes.description: Fit demographic, ancestry and selection models with documented likelihood or simulation methods; diagnose sampling, linkage and demographic confounding.
Derive Wright-Fisher, selection-migration, fixation and linkage models; construct coalescent waiting times and recombination genealogies.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Structural Biology

includes: Biomolecular diffraction, restraints and projection reconstruction

practice: Reconstruct synthetic density and audit an unfamiliar molecular structure using complementary evidence.

outcomes.description: Derive reciprocal-space intensities and Fourier-density relations; explain phase recovery and refine bounded structures against diffraction data.
Implement small projection alignment and reconstruction; validate cryo-EM maps, resolution and molecular models against independent evidence.
Convert multidimensional NMR correlations into assignments and distance restraints; evaluate conformational ensembles and structural ambiguity.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Advanced Inorganic Chemistry

includes: Symmetry and quantitative inorganic bonding

practice: Discriminate electronic assignments for an unfamiliar complex using symmetry and spectral calculations.

outcomes.description: Derive ligand-field and molecular-orbital descriptions; interpret multiplet, magnetic and spectroscopic evidence in coordination compounds.
Construct point-group operations and representations; derive character and projection methods for molecular orbitals and vibrations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Advanced Organic Chemistry

includes: Physical-organic inference and advanced synthetic theory

practice: Defend competing routes to an unfamiliar stereochemical target with mechanism-discriminating experiments.

outcomes.description: Infer transition states and mechanisms from isotope, substituent, rate and stereochemical effects; derive frontier-orbital and pericyclic selection arguments.
Design convergent, asymmetric and photochemical strategies; compare catalyst, selectivity, robustness and material-efficiency tradeoffs.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Dynamics
decks.description: Connect molecular states and chemical motion.

includes: Molecular rate theory and chemical relaxation

practice: Predict rates and relaxation from an unfamiliar energy landscape and discriminate transport limitations.

outcomes.description: Construct molecular partition functions and derive collision and transition-state rates; assess tunneling, recrossing and solvent-friction limits.
Solve finite-state master and reaction-diffusion equations; relate correlation functions to relaxation and time-resolved spectral observations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Computational Chemistry

includes: Electronic workflows, molecular dynamics and free energies

practice: Compare electronic and force-field predictions with separate convergence and sampling budgets.

outcomes.description: Run electronic optimizations, frequencies and reaction paths with basis, correlation, saddle-point and convergence diagnostics.
Derive Newtonian force-field state equations and implement periodic molecular dynamics; develop thermostat, reweighting and thermodynamic-integration procedures with overlap and uncertainty checks.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: General Relativity

includes: Lorentzian geometry, Einstein equations and cosmology

practice: Compute observables in an unfamiliar symmetric metric and assess cosmological assumptions.

outcomes.description: Construct Lorentzian metrics and stress-energy tensors; derive covariant conservation and Einstein equations by bounded action variation.
Solve symmetric vacuum and cosmological models; calculate redshift, lensing, orbital effects, linearized waves and expansion observables.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Inverse Physical Problems

includes: Physical parameter recovery, regularization and experimental design

practice: Recover an unfamiliar source from noisy field observations and design a resolving measurement.

outcomes.description: Derive bounded adjoint sensitivities and information-based design criteria; validate held-out predictions and discriminate model discrepancy from parameter uncertainty.
Construct weighted and Bayesian inverse models; implement sensitivity-based fitting and regularization and diagnose nonuniqueness and posterior uncertainty.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Kinetic Plasma Theory

includes: Kinetic distributions, plasma response and damping

practice: Explain unfamiliar plasma damping data using competing kinetic and fluid descriptions.

outcomes.description: Derive Vlasov and bounded collisional kinetic equations; connect distribution moments to fluid closures and conservation laws.
Calculate linear kinetic response, Landau damping and selected instabilities using explicit contour prescriptions; compare with fluid limits.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Field Theory

includes: Relativistic quantization, scattering and gauge foundations

practice: Calculate an unfamiliar scattering observable with explicit gauge, normalization and renormalization conventions.

outcomes.description: Develop Lorentz representations and scalar, spinor and gauge actions; derive canonical and Gaussian path-integral quantization and propagators.
Derive Feynman rules and low-order cross sections; calculate bounded regularization and renormalization examples and explain symmetry breaking and Standard Model field content.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Many-Body Matter

includes: Interacting quantum models and response

practice: Implement a small interacting lattice model and audit an effective theory against exact spectra.

outcomes.description: Construct second-quantized lattice Hamiltonians; derive mean-field, quasiparticle and representative superconducting, magnetic or topological effective models.
Calculate correlation and Green functions and bounded linear response; compare spectral predictions with implemented small-system diagonalization.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Computational Neuroscience

includes: Conductance, spiking and small neural-network models

practice: Implement a membrane and network model and discriminate mechanisms using unfamiliar spike data.

outcomes.description: Derive and implement conductance, gating and integrate-and-fire equations; analyze excitability, nullclines and numerical stability.
Construct synaptic networks and spike-observation likelihoods; fit bounded models and test coding, plasticity and held-out response predictions.
